I am Mai Vo, and I am supply chain minded. I study supply chain, operations, and analytics, and I graduate in April 2028. I look at every process through three costs: money, time, and opportunity. And I test every fix with two questions: is it effective, and is it efficient? On the Asia Sourcing trip, I evaluated suppliers at sixteen sites across four Asian markets, built a tracking database from more than eighty entities, and modeled landed cost for a transaction over ten thousand dollars. At IDFL in Viet Nam, I lead a rebrand through twenty cross-functional workshops, rewrote two standard operating procedures, and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot that cuts response times by three days. At Brigham Young University-Hawaii, I lead a five-person team building Excel time-study models for eight grounds areas, to replace gut feeling staffing with measured labor hours. I also automated reminders at the Office of Information Technology, lifting participation from about fifty percent to eighty percent, and I now manage projects at the Willes Center for International Entrepreneurship. I am here to learn how operations run at Crane in Sumner, and I will follow the Summer 2027 intern process when it starts in January. Thank you for your time.
